subject: maths
title: Year 1 Position and Direction
seo_title: Year 1 Position and Direction Worksheets: Left and Right, Turns and Position Words (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Describe position, direction and movement, including whole, half, quarter and three-quarter turns.
meta_desc: Free Year 1 position and direction worksheets for the National Curriculum: on, under, above, next to, behind and between, left and right, first, second and third, whole, half, quarter and three-quarter turns, and moving on a grid. 100 picture questions with an answer key.
key_big: Position words tell us where something is. A half turn makes you face the opposite way; a whole turn brings you back.
key_sub: Left and right are the sides of your left and right hands. First is nearest the finish. On a grid, count the moves, not the square you start on.
body_html:
Where is it?

Position words tell us where something is.

Between means in the middle of two things.

Left and right

Look at the picture. Left is the side of your left hand. Right is the side of your right hand.

First, second, third

In a race, the one nearest the finish is first. Then second, third, fourth. The one at the back is last.

Turns

A whole turn goes all the way round. A half turn makes you face the opposite way. A quarter turn is like a square corner. A three-quarter turn is 3 quarter turns.

TurnQuarter turnsYou face
quarter turn1to the side
half turn2the opposite way
three-quarter turn3the other side
whole turn4the same way again

Clockwise is the way the hands of a clock turn. Anticlockwise is the other way.

Moving on a grid

Count the moves, not the square you start on.

Example 1

Ava faces the tree. She makes a half turn. What does she face now?

A half turn makes you face the opposite way. The pond is opposite the tree.

Answer: the pond

Example 2

5 children are in a line. Leo is third. How many children are in front of him?

First and second are in front of Leo. Do not count Leo.

Answer: 2 children

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up left and rightHold up your hands. Your left hand makes an L shape
Saying on when it is aboveOn touches. Above has a gap
Mixing up a half turn and a quarter turnHalf turn: face the opposite way. Quarter turn: face the side
Counting the start squareCount the moves: 1, 2, 3 ...
Counting first from the wrong endFirst is nearest the finish or the front of the line

faq.q: What do Year 1 children learn about position and direction?
faq.a: They use words like on, under, above, below, next to, between, in front of and behind, and left and right. They also learn whole, half, quarter and three-quarter turns.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn left and right?
faq.a: Hold up both hands with the fingers up and thumbs out. The left hand makes an L shape. Play games like “touch your left ear” and say left and right on walks.

faq.q: What is a quarter turn for Year 1?
faq.a: A quarter turn is a turn to the side, like a square corner. Two quarter turns make a half turn, and four make a whole turn.

faq.q: What is the difference between a half turn and a whole turn?
faq.a: After a half turn you face the opposite way. After a whole turn you go all the way round and face the same way as at the start.

items.q: Where is the ball?
items.e: The ball is on the table. It touches the top of the table. Above would mean higher, with a gap.

items.q: Where is the cat?
items.e: The cat is under the table. The table top is over it.

items.q: Where is the balloon?
items.e: The balloon is above the table. It is higher than the table, but it does not touch it. It is not on the table.

items.q: Where is the teddy?
items.e: The teddy is next to the table. It is at the side, close to it.

items.q: Where is the duck?
items.e: The duck is on the table. It touches the top of the table. Above would mean higher, with a gap.

items.q: Where is the car?
items.e: The car is under the table. The table top is over it.

items.q: Where is the ball?
items.e: We can see all of the ball. It hides part of the box. It is nearer to us. It is in front of the box.

items.q: Where is the teddy?
items.e: The box hides part of the teddy. The teddy is further back. It is behind the box.

items.q: Where is the duck?
items.e: We can see all of the duck. It hides part of the box. It is nearer to us. It is in front of the box.

items.q: Where is the cat?
items.e: The box hides part of the cat. The cat is further back. It is behind the box.

items.q: What is between the ball and the car?
items.e: Between means in the middle. The cat is in the middle of the ball and the car.

items.q: What is between the teddy and the star?
items.e: Find the teddy and the star. The duck is in the middle of them.

items.q: Where is the duck?
c: between the book and the ball
items.e: The duck has the book on one side and the ball on the other. It is between them.

items.q: What is just above the cat?
items.e: Look up from the cat. The shelf above has the ball. The duck is below the cat.

items.q: What is just below the apple?
items.e: Look down from the apple. The shelf below has the ball. The teddy is above the apple.

items.q: Where is the duck?
items.e: The duck is on the top shelf. The car is on the shelf under it. So the duck is above the car.

items.q: Where is the teddy?
items.e: The teddy is on the bottom shelf. The ball is on the shelf over it. So the teddy is below the ball.

items.q: Which picture shows the ball under the table?
items.e: Picture D. The ball is under the table top. In one picture the green apple is under the table, not the ball.

items.q: Which picture shows the cat behind the box?
items.e: Picture A. The box hides part of the cat, so the cat is behind the box.

items.q: Which picture shows the teddy on the table?
items.e: Picture C. The teddy touches the top of the table, so it is on the table.

items.q: Which toy is at the left end?
items.e: Your left hand is on the left side. The duck is at the left end.

items.q: Which toy is at the right end?
items.e: The right end is on the side of your right hand. It is the ball.

items.q: Which toy is at the right end?
items.e: Right is the side of your right hand. The car is at the right end. The teddy is at the left end.

items.q: Which toy is at the left end?
items.e: Left is the side of your left hand. The book is at the left end.

items.q: Which toy is 2nd from the left?
items.e: Start at the left end. Count 1, 2: the ball, the cat. The 2nd toy is the cat.

items.q: Which toy is 2nd from the right?
items.e: Start at the right end. Count 1, 2: the ball, the book. The 2nd toy is the book.

items.q: Which toy is 3rd from the left?
items.e: Start at the left end. Count 1, 2, 3: the apple, the duck, the book. The 3rd toy is the book.

items.q: Which toy is 3rd from the right?
items.e: Start at the right end. Count 1, 2, 3: the cat, the apple, the duck. The 3rd toy is the duck.

items.q: Which toy is 4th from the left?
items.e: Start at the left end. Count 1, 2, 3, 4: the star, the book, the cat, the ball. The 4th toy is the ball.

items.q: Which toy is 2nd from the right?
items.e: Start at the right end. Count 1, 2: the book, the car. The 2nd toy is the car.

items.q: What is just to the right of the duck?
items.e: Find the duck. Look to the right of it. The toy just to the right is the apple.

items.q: What is just to the left of the car?
items.e: Find the car. Look to the left of it. The toy just to the left is the star.

items.q: What is just to the left of the teddy?
items.e: Find the teddy. Look to the left of it. The toy just to the left is the cat.

items.q: What is just to the right of the star?
items.e: Find the star. Look to the right of it. The toy just to the right is the teddy.

items.q: Where is the cat?
c: to the left of the ball
to the right of the ball
items.e: The cat is on the left side of the ball. So it is to the left of the ball.

items.q: Where is the duck?
c: to the left of the apple
to the right of the apple
items.e: The duck is on the right side of the apple. So it is to the right of the apple.

items.q: Where is the teddy?
c: to the left of the book
to the right of the book
items.e: The teddy is on the left side of the book. So it is to the left of the book.

items.q: Which picture shows the cat to the left of the ball?
items.e: Picture B. The cat is on the left side, and the ball is on the right side.

items.q: Which picture shows the car to the right of the apple?
items.e: Picture A. The apple is on the left side and the car is on the right side.

items.q: The ball is 1st from the left. What is it from the right?
items.e: Start at the right end: star 1st, car 2nd, teddy 3rd, ball 4th.

items.q: The cars race to the flag. Which car is first?
items.e: First is the car nearest the flag. That is the blue car. Do not start counting at the wrong end.

items.q: Which car is second?
items.e: Start at the flag. Blue is first, red is second.

items.q: Which car is last?
items.e: Last is the car furthest from the flag. It is the purple car.

items.q: What position is the green car?
items.e: Count from the flag: blue first, red second, green third.

items.q: The flag is on the left. Which car is first?
items.e: The cars race to the left. The orange car is nearest the flag, so it is first.

items.q: What position is the blue car?
items.e: Count from the flag: orange, green, red, blue. Blue is fourth. It is also last.

items.q: Which car is second?
items.e: Count from the flag on the left: orange first, green second.

items.q: Which car is just behind the red car?
items.e: Behind means further from the flag. The car just behind red is green. Blue is in front of red.

items.q: Which car is just in front of the blue car?
items.e: In front means nearer the flag. The car just in front of blue is purple.

items.q: Which car is fourth?
items.e: Count from the flag: yellow 1st, purple 2nd, blue 3rd, green 4th.

items.q: The children wait at the door. Who is first in the line?
items.e: First is nearest the door. That is Ava. Ruby is last.

items.q: Who is third in the line?
items.e: Count from the door: Ava, Leo, Zara.

items.q: What position is Kai?
items.e: Count from the door: Ava 1st, Leo 2nd, Zara 3rd, Kai 4th.

items.q: How many children are in front of Zara?
items.e: Ava and Leo are in front of Zara. That is 2. Do not count Zara herself.

items.q: The door is on the right. Who is last in the line?
items.e: First is nearest the door: Noah. The last one is furthest from the door: Evie.

items.q: Who is just behind Isla?
items.e: Behind Isla means further from the door. That is Jack. Noah is in front of Isla.

items.q: Freya came second in a race. Jack was just in front of her. What position was Jack?
items.e: Just in front of second is first.

items.q: Maya came third in a race. Alfie came just after her. What position was Alfie?
items.e: Just after third comes fourth.

items.q: There are 4 children in a line. Poppy is first. Charlie is last. What position is Charlie?
items.e: There are 4 children, so last is fourth.

items.q: Which word comes just after second?
items.e: first, second, third, fourth, fifth.

sets.title: Whole, half, quarter and three-quarter turns

items.q: The arrow shows a turn. What turn is it?
items.e: The line turns to the side, like a square corner. That is a quarter turn.
The line ends pointing the opposite way. That is a half turn, not a quarter turn.
The arrow goes past the half turn and stops at the side. That is a three-quarter turn: 3 quarter turns.
The arrow goes all the way round, back to the start. That is a whole turn.

items.q: The arrow shows a turn. What turn is it?
items.e: The line turns to the side, like a square corner. That is a quarter turn.
The line ends pointing the opposite way. That is a half turn, not a quarter turn.

items.q: Ava faces the tree. She makes a half turn. What does she face now?
items.e: A half turn makes you face the opposite way. Ava now faces the pond.

items.q: Isla faces the tree. She makes a quarter turn clockwise. What does she face now?
items.e: Clockwise is the way the hands of a clock go. A quarter turn from the tree makes her face the house.

items.q: Lily faces the house. She makes a quarter turn clockwise. What does she face now?
items.e: Clockwise is the way the hands of a clock go. A quarter turn from the house makes her face the pond.

items.q: Grace faces the tree. She makes a three-quarter turn clockwise. What does she face now?
items.e: Turn clockwise, like the hands of a clock, one quarter at a time: house, pond, swings. Grace faces the swings.

items.q: Leo faces the pond. He makes a whole turn. What does he face now?
items.e: A whole turn goes all the way round. Leo faces the pond again.

items.q: Noah faces the tree. He makes a quarter turn anticlockwise. What does he face now?
items.e: Anticlockwise is the other way to the hands of a clock. A quarter turn from the tree makes him face the swings.

items.q: George faces the swings. He makes a half turn. What does he face now?
items.e: A half turn makes you face the opposite way. George now faces the house.

items.q: The arrow turns. What turn did it make?
items.e: Up to down is the opposite way. That is a half turn.

items.q: The arrow turns clockwise. What turn did it make?
items.e: Clockwise from up, one quarter turn points right. That is a quarter turn.

items.q: The arrow turns clockwise. What turn did it make?
items.e: Clockwise from up: right, down, left. That is 3 quarter turns: a three-quarter turn.

items.q: How many quarter turns make a half turn?
items.e: 2 quarter turns make a half turn.

items.q: How many quarter turns make a whole turn?
items.e: 4 quarter turns go all the way round. They make a whole turn.

items.q: Which turn makes you face the same way again?
items.e: A whole turn goes all the way round. You end facing the same way.

items.q: Which turn makes you face the opposite way?
items.e: A half turn makes you face the opposite way, like turning round to look behind you.

sets.title: Moving and turning in real life

items.q: The robot moves 3 squares to the right. What does it land on?
items.e: Do not count the square the robot is on. Count each move: 1, 2, 3. It lands on the apple.

items.q: The robot moves 2 squares to the left. What does it land on?
items.e: Do not count the square the robot is on. Count each move: 1, 2. It lands on the ball.

items.q: The robot moves 2 squares up. What does it land on?
items.e: Do not count the square the robot is on. Count each move: 1, 2. It lands on the star.

items.q: The robot moves 2 squares down. What does it land on?
items.e: Do not count the square the robot is on. Count each move: 1, 2. It lands on the duck.

items.q: The robot moves 4 squares to the right. What does it land on?
items.e: Do not count the square the robot is on. Count each move: 1, 2, 3, 4. It lands on the teddy.

items.q: The robot faces the way of the red arrow. It moves 2 squares forwards. What does it land on?
items.e: Do not count the square the robot is on. Count each move: 1, 2. It lands on the cat.

items.q: The robot faces the way of the red arrow. It moves 3 squares forwards. What does it land on?
items.e: Do not count the square the robot is on. Count each move: 1, 2, 3. It lands on the ball.

items.q: The robot faces the way of the red arrow. It moves 2 squares forwards. What does it land on?
items.e: Do not count the square the robot is on. Count each move: 1, 2. It lands on the apple.

items.q: How many squares must the robot move to the right to reach the apple?
items.e: Count the moves, not the square the robot starts on. It moves 4 squares.

items.q: How many squares must the robot move to the left to reach the star?
items.e: Count the moves, not the square the robot starts on. It moves 3 squares.

items.q: How many squares must the robot move up to reach the duck?
items.e: Count the moves, not the square the robot starts on. It moves 3 squares.

items.q: The robot moves 2 squares to the right. Then it moves 1 square down. What does it land on?
items.e: 2 to the right, then 1 down. It lands on the cat. Up would be the apple.

items.q: The robot faces up. It makes a quarter turn clockwise. Then it moves 2 squares forwards. What does it land on?
items.e: A quarter turn clockwise from up makes it face right. 2 squares to the right is the star.

items.q: Leo sits on a roundabout. It makes a whole turn. Which way does Leo face now?
items.e: A whole turn goes all the way round. Leo faces the same way as at the start.

items.q: Isla is third in the lunch queue. How many children are in front of her?
items.e: First and second are in front of her. That is 2 children. Do not count Isla.

items.q: Noah faces the board. He turns round to face the back of the classroom. What turn did he make?
items.e: Facing the opposite way is a half turn.

items.q: Grace makes a quarter turn. Then she makes another quarter turn. How far has she turned?
items.e: 2 quarter turns make a half turn.

items.q: Kai walks 3 steps forwards. Then he walks 3 steps backwards. Where is he now?
items.e: 3 steps forwards and 3 steps back cancel out. He is back where he started.

items.q: Ruby faces the door. She makes a whole turn. What does she face now?
items.e: A whole turn takes you all the way round. Ruby faces the door again.

items.q: The shop is to the left of the house. Which side of the shop is the house?
items.e: If the shop is on the left of the house, the house is to the right of the shop.
